requirements.evidence: The change cannot run: AppServiceProvider.php:31 calls `Password::defaults()` on `Illuminate\Support\Facades\Password` (the broker, which has no `defaults()`), Login.php:20/40 and Register.php:25/50 declare `submit(): void` yet `return redirect()->route('home')` (fatal 'A void function must not return a value'), and PasswordResetController.php:254 / VerificationController.php:34 extend `Controller` without importing it. Reset-password reveals whether an e-mail exists (PasswordResetController.php:261-266), the login redirect uses `redirect()->route('home')` instead of `intended` (Login.php:40), and `.env.example`/`phpunit.xml` locale pins are absent from the diff.

conventions.evidence: No `#[Validate]` attributes on the public Livewire properties (Login.php:16-18, Register.php:22-25) and no `#[Locked]` for server-only state, contrary to conventions.md:130-137. `Password::defaults` is configured through the wrong facade (AppServiceProvider.php:31). No test files, no CHANGELOG/docs updates, and `use` imports sit after executable code in routes/web.php:13-18.

security.evidence: Forgot-password leaks account existence by returning `trans(Password::INVALID_USER)` in the status flash (PasswordResetController.php:261-266), the login `exists:users,email` rule enumerates users and surfaces the wrong message instead of `auth.failed` (Login.php:27), and the verification action ignores `$id`/`$hash` and verifies whichever user is logged in (VerificationController.php:41-47). No `{!! !!}` or mass-assignment issue found in the shown views.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all; `grep` of change.diff shows only app/, lang/, resources/views/ and routes/ changes. No happy-path, validation, throttle, unauthorized-call or tamper tests exist despite conventions.md:12-21 and 183-185.

simplicity.evidence: PasswordResetController.php:1-250 is a copy-paste dump of dozens of aliased/duplicated imports (e.g. `Validator as ValidatorFacade` at lines 27 and 41, which is a PHP fatal 'name already in use') for a four-method controller, dwarfing the 4 short methods that follow.

readability.evidence: Duplicated imports (PasswordResetController.php:27,41), an empty branch `if (! $user->hasVerifiedEmail() && $user->markEmailAsVerified()) { // do nothing }` (VerificationController.php:42-44), unused imports in LogoutController.php:11-16, and many unused/duplicated aliases throughout make the code hard to follow.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the auth task (routes/web.php:20-39, app/Livewire/Auth/*, app/Http/Controllers/Auth/*, lang/*, resources/views/auth/*); there are no unrelated features or refactors, only the junk import block that is incidental to the task.

issues.explanation: `Password::defaults()` is called on the `Illuminate\Support\Facades\Password` broker facade, which has no such method, so boot() throws a BadMethodCallException on every request and the app never starts.
`submit(): void` returns the result of `redirect()->route('home')`, which is a fatal PHP error, so login is unusable.
`submit(): void` returns the result of `redirect()->route('home')`, a fatal PHP error, so registration is unusable.
Both classes `extend Controller` but never import `Illuminate\Routing\Controller`, so loading them fails with 'Class ...\Controller not found'.
`Validator as ValidatorFacade` (and many other aliases) are imported more than once, which is a PHP fatal 'Cannot use ... because the name is already in use' compile error.
The forgot-password endpoint flashes `trans($response)`, so an unknown e-mail returns the `passwords.user` message and reveals whether an account exists, directly contradicting requirement 5.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for any new behaviour, including the required unauthorized-call and tamper tests, violating the project's test-first rule.
Requirement 8's APP_NAME/APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE entries and the phpunit.xml locale pins are not present in the diff.
The verify action ignores the `$id` and `$hash` route parameters and simply marks the current user verified, so a valid signed link for a different id verifies the wrong account.
The `exists:users,email` validation rule reveals which e-mails are registered and produces a different error than the required `auth.failed`, enabling account enumeration.
The post-login redirect is `redirect()->route('home')` rather than `redirect()->intended(...)`, so the 'intended' URL required by requirement 1 is dropped.
Public user-input properties have no `#[Validate]` attributes as required by the project's Livewire pattern, only an inline `$this->validate()` call.
`verification.verify` has `auth` and `signed` middleware but no `throttle`, while requirement 7 asks for a signed and throttled verification link.
Views reference non-existent keys such as `auth.passwords.email`, `auth.passwords.send` and `auth.email`, so those labels render the raw key instead of translated text.
Authenticated users hitting `login` rely on the framework's default `guest` redirect target (not guaranteed to be `home`), and `verification.notice` has no `auth` middleware.
`use` import statements appear after route definitions instead of at the top of the file, contrary to the sibling style and Pint conventions.
The `if (...) { // do nothing }` block is dead structure that should simply be the conditional call.

review.summary: The change attempts the full auth surface (Livewire login/register, logout, password reset, e-mail verification, pt-BR/en UI strings and routes) but does not work: it misuses the Password facade during boot, has `void` methods returning redirects, controllers that extend an unimported `Controller`, and a PHP-fatal duplicate-import block. On top of that it ships no tests, misses the .env/phpunit locale pins, omits `intended`, and leaks account existence in password reset and login validation, so the pull request must be rejected.
